target_customer: Action sports consumers in 2015 (free iOS and Mac app with paid export); later adventure tourism operators such as skydiving, bungee and rafting companies that sell videos to their customers
problem: Editing raw GoPro, phone or drone footage into a shareable clip takes hours in tools like Final Cut or Premiere; later, tour operators need to capture, edit and sell cinematic media automatically.
business_model: Consumer freemium app (paid saving and watermark removal) in 2015; later B2B service for tour operators with fees collected only once the operator makes sales

founders.name: Mike Allen
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and on the company about page. No background found in sources opened.

founders.name: Mark Godfrey
founders.background_notes: Named as Founder/CTO on the YC page. The company about page captions him as CTA, likely a typo. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: The YC launch post says the app processes footage in about 10 seconds, and TechCrunch says it uses camera acceleration to find action moments and match them to song beats. That is signal processing plus video rendering by a two person team, standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: A consumer auto-edit app was easy to copy and had no network effects or data lock-in. A 2015 trade article cited in search results framed GoPro as likely to add auto-editing itself, which shows the feature was a thin wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GoPro bought the Replay editing app, later rebranded Quik, per an AppleInsider piece. Shred Video later moved away from the consumer app, whose iOS and Mac versions its FAQ says are alive but not in active development.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-07-21) and the YC post frame the pain as hours spent editing action footage in Final Cut or Adobe Premiere; GoPro and drone footage was growing but little of it got edited.

branding.domain_note: Uses the exact .com shredvideo.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Adventure and action sports voice; the about page calls the team video technologists who love video, tech and adventure sports.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself, no merch or community found. Searches for the name mostly return unrelated Shred brands (a fitness app, a film, a surf show).

pivots.from: Free consumer app that auto-edits GoPro, iPhone and drone footage to a song
pivots.to: Automated video and photo systems sold to adventure tourism operators using LiDAR, GPS and smart cameras
pivots.why: Not stated by the company. Exact date not found; the current site and FAQ describe the tour product.

outcome_analysis: Shred Video launched out of Y Combinator in July 2015 as a free consumer auto-editor for action footage, with a reported YC seed of 120,000 dollars. No further funding or press was found. The company is still listed as active but its site now sells automated video systems to adventure tour operators, which suggests the consumer app did not become the business. Reasons for the shift are not public, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Not an outcome conflict: status Active and no exit found. Funding: Xconomy and StartupIntros both state a 120,000 dollar seed; Seedtable shows no rounds. YC's standard deal is recorded as other because the amount is reported. Competitors: the YC launch post and TechCrunch article name none; a Reviewed.com article cited in search names Graava as a similar auto-editing startup but I could not open it to confirm its date, so it is excluded. The Crunchbase and other Shred hits (LA fitness app raising 4M in 2020) are different companies.
